standard.title: Local community change and diversity
standard.description: causes and effects of changes to the local community, and how people who may be from diverse backgrounds have contributed to these changes
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y2 (AC9HS2K01-K02): Students explained local significance and how technological developments changed daily life. They understand continuity and change and source-based investigation.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain causes and effects of changes to the local community and describe how people from diverse backgrounds have contributed to those changes.

nodes.label: Identifying community changes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify changes to the local community over time by examining sources such as photographs, newspapers and oral histories.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two changes to the local community using at least two different source types.
nodes.typical_width: Explore photographs, newspapers, oral histories, diaries and letters to investigate how aspects of the local community (transport, environment, technology) have changed; compare photographs from past and present of specific locations to identify change and continuity.
wider: Investigate how an aspect of local community life changed from the time of European settlement to the present day
Compare change rates across different aspects of the community (natural environment vs built environment vs social life)
nodes.hinge_reason: Students must be able to identify specific changes before analysing their causes and effects — naming the change is prerequisite to explaining it.

response_modes.reason: Build a class inventory of local changes across multiple domains using sources before moving to causal analysis.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two changes to the local community
Uses at least two source types as evidence

nodes.label: Causes and effects of change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why a change happened in the local community and what happened as a result.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain one cause and one effect of a specific change to the local community.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate reasons for change in the local community (why change was brought about) and what happened because of it; connect causes to effects for at least two changes.
wider: Investigate multiple causes for a single change and rank them by importance
Trace a chain of effects from one community change through to present day consequences
nodes.hinge_reason: Cause-effect reasoning is new at Year 3 — students who cannot identify causes cannot connect them to diverse contributors in Node 3.

response_modes.reason: Model cause-effect reasoning explicitly using 'because' and 'as a result' sentence frames before expecting independent causal analysis.

success_criteria: States at least one cause of a community change
States at least one effect of that change

nodes.label: Diverse contributors to community change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify individuals and groups from diverse backgrounds who have contributed to the community's development and describe their contribution.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one individual or group from a diverse background who contributed to the local community and describe their contribution.
nodes.typical_width: Identify individuals and groups from diverse backgrounds (economic, social, cultural, civic, environmental) who have contributed to community development; connect their contributions to specific changes in the community.
wider: Compare contributions from First Nations Australian community members with those of settlers and migrants to the same local area
Investigate how a previously unrecognised contributor's story is now being told and why their recognition matters

response_modes.reason: The more diverse the range of contributors examined, the richer the understanding of community complexity — seek contributors across cultural, economic and civic domains.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Contributors from diverse backgrounds reveal that community change is multi-authored — this directly challenges monocultural narratives of local history.
success_criteria: Names at least one contributor from a diverse background
Describes their contribution and connects it to a community change
